subject: Scheduling maintenance window + temporary SLA accommodation request — GalaxyTech reserved GPUs
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@galaxytech.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: scheduled maintenance and SLA accommodation for reserved capacity

Hi Irene —

We're planning a planned maintenance window for our infra on the night of Jun 5 (UTC). That maintenance will impact network connectivity to the VPC hosting our Redwood Dedicated pool (4 reserved GPUs, A100). We want to minimize customer impact and are exploring options with Redwood:

- Can Redwood provide a short, pre-agreed mitigation (temporary SLA accommodation / soft guarantee) for the 30–45 minute window so our internal ops can proceed without large downstream fallout?
- During the window, what will happen to in-flight requests queued at the Redwood pool? Will they queue, be rejected, or can they be routed automatically to the hosted tier?
- We need deeper observability hooks during the window (per-request trace id, TTL on KV cache entries, and a dedicated log stream).

I've attached a draft maintenance plan outlining the timing and expected load profile (typical daytime: 1.5k tokens/s; maintenance: brief spike to ~2.2k tokens/s during drain). Can you confirm feasibility and what temporary service-level language you can offer (throughput / uptime) so I can get internal sign-off?

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Head of Platform Reliability
GalaxyTech
Attachment: maintenance-plan-galaxytech-v1.pdf
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@galaxytech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 28 May 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: scheduled maintenance and SLA accommodation for reserved capacity

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for the heads up and the plan — I reviewed the PDF. We can work with you on a short, scoped accommodation for a scheduled maintenance event. A couple of clarifying questions so we can propose concrete language:

1) Exact UTC window you want Redwood to treat as the maintenance window (proposal: 2026-06-05 02:00–02:45 UTC).
2) During the window, do you prefer:
   - A) Drain existing requests and reject new requests to the Dedicated pool (400 error) with automatic routing to our Hosted tier (will incur hosted billing), or
   - B) Allow requests to queue up to configured queue depth and preserve order (may increase tail latency), or
   - C) Immediate reroute to pre-warmed hosted fallback (if capacity available).
3) Are the reserved GPUs single tenant (private VPC) or connected via our private control plane (affects failover capability)?

If you confirm (1–3) I'll draft temporary SLA wording and a short runbook (observability hooks, tracing, a dedicated log stream and retention) and loop in Product Ops to agree on fallback routing.

Proposed interim: Redwood will target preserving >=95% of committed steady-state throughput during the 45-minute window by routing overflow to Hosted fallback where possible, provide a dedicated log stream and 1-minute aggregated metrics for the window, and offer a one-time service credit if we fail to meet the accommodation. I'll need Ben and Jordan to confirm from pricing/ops side — tagging them here.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachment: none
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 29 May 2026 09:30:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Request: scheduled maintenance and SLA accommodation for reserved capacity — internal ops + pricing input

Folks — forwarding GalaxyTech's request. Key details: 4 reserved A100s, expected steady throughput ~1.5k tokens/s, drain spike ~2.2k tokens/s; proposed window 2026-06-05 02:00–02:45 UTC.

Questions for ops/pricing:
- Routing behavior: Jordan, can we commit to automatic routing to Hosted fallback for the window? If so, what's the estimated headroom required to keep >=95% throughput? If hosted capacity doesn't exist, do we fallback to queueing?
- Billing/credits: Ben, what is reasonable on the commercial side for a one-time accommodation (service credit or temporary adjustment of throughput commitment)? GalaxyTech is asking for pre-agreed language to speed their internal approval.
- Observability: Evelyn, ops wants per-request trace forwarding + 1-minute aggregated metrics for the window. I've attached sample logs they asked for.

Proposal I'm drafting for customer:
- Redwood will enable automatic overflow routing to Hosted fallback for this window.
- If Hosted fallback is not available for bursts, we will queue up to 120s per-request and then return 503 with guidance to retry.
- Redwood will provide a dedicated telemetry stream and 90-day retention for events tied to the maintenance window.
- If Redwood fails to meet the >=95% throughput target for the window, GalaxyTech will receive a one-time credit equal to 10% of that month's Dedicated capacity fees.

Jordan: can you validate the queue depth/timeout and whether 120s is a safe bound (we don't want long-running KV locking).
Ben: I'm trying to avoid a long redline fight; a 10% credit (one-time) seems reasonable for a scheduled event. Thoughts?

Attachments: observability-sample-logs.txt

—Irene
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@galaxytech.com>, GalaxyTech SRE <sre@galaxytech.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Confirmed: maintenance window 2026-06-05 UTC + temporary SLA accommodation summary

Hi Daniel —

Thanks for confirming the details over the call earlier. Per our conversation, Redwood will proceed with the following for the scheduled maintenance on 2026-06-05: 02:00–02:45 UTC (45 minutes):

1) Temporary accommodation (scoped):
   - Target: preserve >=95% of GalaxyTech's committed steady-state throughput for the Dedicated pool during the 45-minute window.
   - Mechanism: Redwood will attempt automatic overflow routing to pre-warmed Hosted fallback instances where available. If fallback capacity is exhausted, Redwood will queue requests up to 120s per-request then return 503 with retry guidance.

2) Queueing & failover behavior:
   - In-flight requests at the start of the window will be drained for up to 120s; new requests will be routed to Hosted fallback when available.
   - We will not hold requests indefinitely; the 120s timeout is to bound tail latency and avoid KV cache contention.

3) Observability & runbook:
   - We'll provide a dedicated telemetry stream for the window (per-request trace id, aggregated 1-minute metrics, and event logs).
   - Runbook link and the temporary-sla wording are attached. Please review and confirm by EOD Tue (2026-06-01) so we can finalize the DocuSign.

4) Commercials:
   - One-time credit: if Redwood fails to meet the >=95% target for the covered window, GalaxyTech will receive a one-time credit equal to 10% of the month’s Dedicated capacity fee (applied to the next billing cycle).

Attachments: redwood-temp-sla-runbook-v1.pdf
Links: https://docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=1234-abcd

Please reply with any small edits; if you need further buffering on throughput we can discuss pre-warming additional fallback capacity for that night (additional hosted pre-warm will be billed).

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
